text:
The goaltending story in St. Louis changed quietly this month: Joel Hofer has taken the starting job from Jordan Binnington. It's been the right call so far. Hofer is +9.8 goals saved above expected with a .920 save rate, and over his last five starts he's 4-1-0 and stopping hard shots at .921. The Blues have won four straight, including a comeback from three goals down against Edmonton on Saturday, and they've scored 27 goals in that run.

That last number is the warning. The Blues took 49% of the expected goals during the streak, the quality of chances each side gets, and finished 27 goals on 14.9 expected. Jimmy Snuggerud has goals in three straight, Robert Thomas has ten points in four games, and Jake Neighbours tied a franchise record with five assists in a game. Logan Mailloux, eight points in seven games, is the one our numbers call earned: his chances are up too. Connor McMichael is out, so Aleksanteri Kaskimaki has his spot beside Pavel Buchnevich and Mason McTavish.

The Islanders run on a similar engine with a better goalie. Ilya Sorokin is +10.8 this season and .932 over his last five starts, and the team's +7 goal difference sits on top of -9.1 expected goals. Goaltending (13.0 above expected) is doing most of that lifting. Kyle Palmieri went on injured reserve after getting hurt on Monday, which opens minutes for Victor Eklund. Casey Cizikas just played his 1,000th game, Mathew Barzal is back, and Matthew Schaefer, the second-year defenseman who is the face of this team's future, is the one we would watch, at 73% for a point.

On paper this is about as even as games get: both teams at 50% of five-on-five expected goals, our numbers at 2.94 expected goals for St. Louis and 3.04 for the Islanders. Both are on the playoff bubble, the Blues at 48% and the Islanders at 40%. With two goalies this sharp, the margins could come down to one chance.
headline: Two hot goalies, and a Blues team riding its finish
